title: Spec: skillz — skills manager CLI/TUI
description:
## Problem Statement

I work across many projects, each with its own set of agent skills. Some skills are Upstream (from other people's GitHub repos), some are Authored by me, some are Forked (started Upstream or Tool-Provided, then tweaked), and some arrive as Tool-Provided globals from tools I install. When I start a new project I often copy skills by hand. That is messy: I forget where a skill lived, copies diverge across Managed Projects, and if I keep skills only as laptop globals, collaborators on a Project never get them. I want a single tool — **skillz** — that keeps Libraries as the union catalog of skills I (or my team/company) use, lets Managed Projects select and Lock Installations from those Libraries, and makes discovery, updates, Drift, and Promote straightforward — including a workplace flow where Library review can lag Project shipping.

## Solution

**skillz** is a CLI (with a future TUI) that replaces Skillfile in my workflow. It manages one or more Libraries (Personal, team, or company), registers Managed Projects (and a user-global `~/.agents/skills` scope) with ordered Library Bindings, and uses Locks so lasting Installations track Catalog Entries. Day-to-day editing and new-skill tryout happen **in the Project (or user) skills directory**; **`libcommit`** formalizes tested Installations into the Library workflow (new Catalog Entry, Library Branch Lock, or Overlay Fork). Discovery includes `skillz list --tag TAG`. git pre-commit and `jj push-with-checks` gate publishing Drift unless explicitly allowed. External Projects are observe/import only. Install scope is intentionally narrow — not Skillfile parity.

Agreed command-level usage is in `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md` and summarized under **Usage Flows** below.

## User Stories

1. As a solo developer, I want a Personal Library that is the union of skills I keep via libcommit from Managed use, so I always know what I standardize on.
2. As a solo developer, I want to record Authored Skills as Owned Entries, so my custom skills have a source of truth outside any one Project.
3. As a solo developer, I want Upstream Skills as Catalog Entries (source + Lock) without owning their content, so the Library stays a complete union without vendoring the internet.
4. As a solo developer, I want to Fork an Upstream or Tool-Provided skill into an Owned Entry when I edit it for keeps, so my tweaks are first-class Library content.
5. As a solo developer, I want Tool-Provided skills left out of the Library until I libcommit/promote them, so globals do not silently pollute the catalog.
6. As a library owner, I want to assign Tags to Catalog Entries, so I can discover skills by topic or toolchain.
7. As a library owner, I want `skillz list` (with filters such as `--tag TAG`), so I can find skills without remembering which Project last used them.
8. As a library owner, I want to search/list across bound Libraries for a Managed Project, so selection respects binding order and availability.
9. As a developer, I want to register a Project as Managed with an ordered list of Library Bindings, so skillz knows where Catalog Entries may come from.
10. As a developer, I want Library Bindings to be read-only or writable, so I can install from a company Library without being able to mutate it.
11. As a developer, I want to try a newly authored or fetched skill in my Project first, then `libcommit` it into a Library, so I test before the union catalog changes.
12. As a developer, I want skillz to materialize an Installation and record a Lock after add/libcommit, so the Project has pinned, reproducible skill content.
13. As a developer, I want Installations committed in the Project repo, so collaborators receive skills on clone without needing my Libraries.
14. As a collaborator, I want to clone a Managed Project and have skill files present, so agents work without running skillz first.
15. As a developer, I want to bump a Lock and reinstall when a Library entry advances, so Projects stay intentionally current.
16. As a developer, I want a Drift Report across Managed Projects, so I can see Installations that disagree with their Locks or with Library main line.
17. As a developer, I want Drift gates and reports to offer libcommit / Branch Lock / Overlay Fork / Promote as explicit next actions, so nothing silently merges into a Library.
18. As a developer, I want to Promote a skill change into a writable Library main line, so lasting shared edits land in the right source of truth.
19. As a developer in a workplace, I want `libcommit` to create a Library Branch Lock from my tested Installation, so I can ship the Project before main-line approval with an honest Lock.
20. As a developer in a workplace, I want a report of Managed Projects whose Locks are not on Library main line, so pre-merge usage is visible.
21. As a developer with a fully read-only Library, I want Overlay Fork into a writable bound Library via libcommit, so I can still ship Project-local skill changes honestly.
22. As a developer, I want External Projects (other people's clones) to be observable without forced Library membership, so skillz does not rewrite foreign repos.
23. As a developer, I want to explicitly import a skill from an External Project into a Library, so useful finds can join the union on purpose.
24. As a team lead, I want a shared team or company Library using the same skillz model, so the workplace uses one tool shape.
25. As a team member, I want my Managed Project to bind company → team → personal with precedence, so name conflicts resolve predictably.
26. As a Library maintainer, I want Promote / libcommit into a company Library to require an explicit writable target, so personal drift never silently writes company content.
27. As a developer starting a new Managed Project, I want to select skills already in Libraries via skillz list/add, so I stop hand-copying from old Projects.
28. As a developer, I want the Project skills directory to default to `.agents/skills` but be overridable (e.g. `.claude/skills`), so skillz fits my agent layout.
29. As a developer, I want to manage `~/.agents/skills` with the same skillz model (`skillz user …`), so user-global skills are not a separate ad-hoc mess.
30. As a developer migrating from Skillfile, I want import (including `-i` TUI adopt) into Catalog Entries + Locks, so I can leave Skillfile behind.
31. As a developer, I want a CLI named `skillz` as the primary interface, so I learn one tool.
32. As a developer, I want a future TUI over the same command API, so discovery, import adopt, and Drift review are pleasant.
33. As a developer, I want `skillz status` for a Managed Project or `--user`, so I can see Bindings, Installations, Locks, and Drift at a glance.
34. As a developer, I want `skillz list --tag` to accept repeated flags and comma-separated lists, so filtering matches how I think about Tags.
35. As a developer, I want list to show all Binding matches in precedence order by default, with optional `--dedupe`, so I can see overlays.
36. As a developer, I want `skillz add --tag …` and `-i` multi-select, so I can pull many Library skills at once.
37. As a developer, I want `skillz fetch github:owner/repo SKILLNAME` to find nested skills, so Pocock-style layouts work.
38. As a developer, I want warnings (and `--with-deps`) when a skill references sibling skills (e.g. grill-with-docs → grilling, domain-modeling), so dependency graphs are less surprising.
39. As a developer, I want git pre-commit to block committing drifting skill files unless I allow Drift, so testing locally does not accidentally publish dishonest Locks.
40. As a developer on jj, I want `jj push-with-checks` (not `skillz push`) to drift-check before `jj git push`, so ordinary pushes stay normal and skill gates sit at the share boundary.
41. As a developer, I want `libcommit` as the verb that turns a tested Installation into Library + Lock state, so edit/add/new share one formalization step.
42. As an agent implementing skillz, I want one application command API as the test seam, so CLI and TUI share behavior.
43. As a Library owner, I want Libraries themselves to be ordinary versioned repos, so review/branch/PR workflows reuse existing source control.
44. As a developer, I want skillz to refuse to treat a Project as Managed until Bindings are configured, so External vs Managed stays explicit.
45. As a developer, I want to remove a skill from a Managed Project (Installation + Lock) without deleting it from the Library, so Projects can drop skills while the union catalog remains.
46. As a developer, I want to see which Managed Projects use a given Catalog Entry, so impact of a Library change is visible before I bump Locks.
47. As a developer, I want failed installs/libcommits to leave Project state consistent, so recovery is clear.
48. As a workplace admin, I want read-only Bindings to still allow install and list, so consumers are not blocked from discovery.

## Usage Flows

Canonical transcripts: `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md`.

### A — Library bootstrap
`library init` / `library add` / `library list`. Registry is **user-global** name → local path. Committed Project Bindings use shared **name + remote URL**. VCS inferred (`.jj/` → jj, else git).

### B — New Managed Project
`project init --bind …` writes Bindings + empty Locks; default `--skills-dir .agents/skills` (overridable). No skills installed yet. Hooks installed.

### B2 — User-global scope
`user init --bind …` manages `~/.agents/skills` with the same model; config/Locks in user skillz state.

### C — Convert existing Project
`project import --dry-run` / `--from skillfile` / `--adopt-local` / `-i` TUI per-skill upstream|authored|skip. Keep matching files; leftovers are Drift candidates. `user import` for home skills.

### D — Discovery
`list` with `--library` / `--user` / `--tag` (repeated and/or comma-separated, AND). Default: show all Binding hits in precedence order; `--dedupe` optional.

### E — Add
- **E1** already in Library: `add` / `add --tag` / `-i` / `--with-deps`.
- **E2/E3** new Upstream or Authored: **Project-first** via `fetch` / `new` into skills dir → test → **`libcommit --as upstream|authored`** into a writable Library (creates Catalog Entry + Lock). Until libcommit = Drift.

### F — Edit / libcommit / Promote
Edit Installation in place; `libcommit` → Branch Lock or Overlay Fork + update Lock; `promote` → Library main; `lock --main` after merge. git pre-commit blocks Drift; jj uses **`jj push-with-checks`**. Escape: `--allow-drift` / `SKILLZ_ALLOW_DRIFT=1`. No `skillz push` as jj entrypoint.

## Implementation Decisions

### Product name and interfaces
- Tool name: **skillz**. v1 CLI; TUI later on the same application command API.
- Replace Skillfile (ADR 0001); narrow install scope; no Skillfile parity.

### Domain rules
- Library = union catalog (Owned + Upstream references) for skills you libcommit/keep.
- Managed Project Bindings: ordered name+url+writability; local registry resolves path.
- Installations committed in Project skills dir (default `.agents/skills`).
- User-global scope: `~/.agents/skills`.
- Edit/new tryout in Installation; **libcommit** formalizes; **Promote** = main-line.
- Branch Lock primary; Overlay Fork fallback (ADR 0002).
- Drift never silent-synced.

### Discovery and deps
- Tags; list filters; no default dedupe.
- Dep heuristics including Pocock `grill-with-docs` pattern; `--with-deps`.

### Metadata (ADR 0003)
- Project: `PROJECT/.skillz/skillz.toml` + `skillz.lock`; Installations in `skills_dir` (default `.agents/skills`).
- User registry: `~/.config/skillz/registry.toml` (Library name→path; Managed Project paths for Drift).
- User scope: `~/.config/skillz/user.toml` + `user.lock`; Installations in `~/.agents/skills`.
- Library repo: `library.toml` + Owned trees under e.g. `skills/`.
- Upstream `source`: `github:owner/repo[/path][@rev]` string in CLI and TOML (not structured fields).

### Architecture / test seam / stack (ADR 0004)
- Rust binary + `skillz-core` lib (application command API = test seam) with temp filesystem fixtures.
- `clap`; TOML via `toml`/`toml_edit`; shell out to `git`/`jj`.
- TUI later: `ratatui` + `crossterm`; not FrankenTUI for v1; thin UI boundary for a possible later swap.
- Libraries as normal git/jj repos; skillz lock format (not Skillfile.lock).

### Hooks
- git pre-commit on skill paths.
- jj: repo-local alias `jj push-with-checks` only (not `skillz push`).

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior of the application command API with fixture Libraries + Managed Projects (+ user-scope temp home).
- Cover: init/bind; import/-i; list tags & dedupe off/on; add from Library; fetch/new → libcommit; edit → libcommit Branch Lock; Overlay Fork; drift gates allow/deny; --with-deps warning path for grill-with-docs-like bodies; read-only library rejects libcommit target.
- CLI argv thin; TUI later. No prior art in-repo (greenfield).

## Out of Scope

- Skillfile coexistence layer; Skillfile-style long-lived patch pins as happy path.
- Silent cron sync into Libraries.
- Auto-Managing every clone under ~/code.
- Auto-import all Tool-Provided globals.
- Full multi-platform install matrix.
- Marketplace product; company auth beyond git hosting.
- TUI in the first vertical slice (API must allow it); FrankenTUI as v1 TUI backend.
- `skillz push` as the jj push command.
- Perfect dependency graphs from prose.

## Further Notes

- Glossary: `CONTEXT.md`.
- ADRs: `0001-replace-skillfile`, `0002-branch-lock-over-patches`, `0003-metadata-layout-and-source-strings`, `0004-rust-stack-ratatui-not-frankentui`.
- Usage/tech annex: `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md`.
- This repo uses jj + Beads (`br`, prefix `z`).
- Open polish: whether `libcommit` auto-chooses Overlay Fork vs requiring a flag; GitHub auth/`gh` vs raw git for private Upstream.
